title: The Beam variant

full_text:
Two country laborers were walking toward the city market when one of them noticed a tiny speck of dust clinging to the shoulder of a passing traveler. He pointed and laughed loudly, mocking the traveler's untidy appearance before the entire crowd.

A wise elder sitting by the town gates overheard the mockery. He stepped forward and placed a massive wooden oak timber beam directly across the scorner's own neck, bending him double under its crushing weight.

"Why do you put this heavy beam upon my neck?" cried the struggling laborer in agony.

The elder answered with quiet authority: "You laugh at a tiny speck of dust on another man's shoulder, yet you are blind to the colossal timber of arrogance and pride that crushes your own soul. Learn to remove the beam from your own heart before you mock the speck in your neighbor's eye."

Humbled and ashamed, the laborer begged for forgiveness, learning that true dignity lies in self-reflection rather than malicious fault-finding.
moral: Examine your own massive flaws before presuming to critique the small errors of others.
